records.title: The Makueni County Sand Conservation and Utilization Act, 2015
records.titleEn: The Makueni County Sand Conservation and Utilization Act, 2015
records.publisher: County Government of Makueni (Makueni County Gazette Supplement)
records.dateEvidence: Source page: Date of Assent: 13th February, 2015
records.location: Makueni County
records.summary: The Makueni County Sand Conservation and Utilization Act, 2015 creates the Makueni County Sand Conservation and Utilization Authority, sub-county committees and sand resource user associations, and licenses sand harvesters and dealers. It allows harvesting and transport only between 6am and 6pm, with offenders liable to two years' imprisonment or a fine of 200,000 shillings or both. Riverbed harvesting must retain a sand reserve for water retention, is barred on riverbanks, and is banned within one hundred metres of infrastructure such as bridges. Sand revenue is split 50% to a conservation fund, 25% to the Authority, 20% to the county government and 5% to the local community.
records.limitations: Original 2015 text as gazetted; later amendments not reviewed. The PDF is a scanned gazette with an OCR text layer, so string matching may need whitespace normalisation. Date is the date of assent.

records.location: Laikipia County, Laikipia North sub-county, Mukogodo division, border of Kurikuri and Makurian group ranches
records.summary: The Laikipia North sub-county security committee banned sand harvesting on a section of land disputed by two communities, and assistant commissioner Benedict Nduva said anyone caught harvesting would be prosecuted. The Yiaku community of Kurikuri Group Ranch in Mukogodo division, led by Lax Manasseh, protested at the border with Makurian group ranch. records.title: Machakos bans sand mining to save dying rivers
records.titleEn: Machakos bans sand mining to save dying rivers
records.location: Machakos County; Masinga, Yatta, Mwala, Kathiani and Kangundo; Mwitasyano River, Yatta
records.summary: The Star reported that the Machakos County assembly passed a law banning riverbed sand harvesting; under the Sand Harvesting Act 2014, licensed groups may harvest only at designated sites at least 50 metres from rivers and no deeper than six feet. County Environment Officer Isaac Kimitei blamed harvesting for drying riverbeds, road damage, drug abuse and school dropouts, citing one scooper buried alive in Kangundo and two in Masinga the previous year. He said restoration orders were issued in Kangundo and five illegal harvesting cases prosecuted in Mwala and Machakos. Ten per cent of collected revenue goes to the committee and associations. Masinga, Yatta, Mwala, Kathiani and Kangundo are most affected.

records.title: Why hunger for resource is a threat to environment conservation
records.titleEn: Why hunger for resource is a threat to environment conservation
records.location: Homa Bay County, Rachuonyo North sub-county (Kobuya and Kobala), Karachuonyo constituency; lakeshore beaches Nyakwara, Sindo, Gingo, Kakione and Kaswanga
records.summary: The Star reports that demand from Oyugis, Homa Bay Town and Kisii has made sand harvesting an alternative livelihood for youths and women in Homa Bay, destroying lakeshore riparian areas, rivers and farms. Environment director John Maniafu said farm harvesting in Kobuya and Kobala is more destructive than riparian harvesting, that houses in Karachuonyo stand in deep pits, and that Kenya Power cut supply where poles were left hanging. He said beaches such as Nyakwara, Sindo, Gingo, Kakione and Kaswanga are at risk, and that harvesters are not organised in groups, contrary to the National Sand Harvesting Guidelines' sub-county committee structure.

records.title: Sand transporters in Kajiado warned against overloading
records.titleEn: Sand transporters in Kajiado warned against overloading
records.location: Kajiado County; Kajiado-Isara road; Eselenkei River; Mashuuru sub-county
records.summary: Kajiado County Commissioner Joshua Nkanatha warned sand transporters on the Kajiado-Isara road against overloading, KNA reported. He said the 68 kilometre low-volume seal road linking Kajiado to Loitoktok is limited to vehicles of 10 tonnes, but trucks carrying sand from Eselenkei River are loaded beyond this, forcing the contractor to redo 16 kilometres. Three lorries overloaded with sand were impounded and their drivers arrested during an inspection of the Sh. 3 billion road. He said transporters ferry sand at night and remove number plates to evade police. More than 200 trucks carrying Eselenkei sand use the road daily, with Mashuuru supplying Nairobi, Makueni and Machakos.
records.limitations: Official statements; transporters dispute the road's design. Focus is road damage rather than river impacts.

records.title: Contractor threatens to stop Lapset road project over Kitui tax
records.titleEn: Contractor threatens to stop Lapset road project over Kitui tax
records.location: Kitui County; Kibwezi-Kitui-Migwani road; Athi River border with Makueni County
records.summary: Kitui County demanded Sh132 million from a Chinese contractor building the Kibwezi-Kitui-Migwani road for ballast and sand taken locally, including from rivers up to the Athi River border with Makueni, and blocked its access to local materials, The Star reported. The contractor threatened to halt works and said the levy was not in its contract. County commissioner John Ondego said the county framed the invoice as payment for sand and ballast obtained below six feet underground, and that the development committee could not tell whether national or county government owns sand in rivers. He said a similar invoice went to the Thwake Dam contractor.

records.title: Sand harvesting a threat to agricultural land, NECC says
records.titleEn: Sand harvesting a threat to agricultural land, NECC says
records.location: National scope; cases cited in Homa Bay, Makueni, West Pokot (Mtembur and Kanyarkwar), Machakos and Trans Nzoia
records.summary: National Environmental Complaints Committee secretary John Chumo said sand demand was pushing harvesters from depleted riverbeds onto farmland, citing NECC investigations in Homa Bay, Makueni, West Pokot, Machakos and Trans Nzoia. He said on one five-acre farm only an acre remained in production. The Star notes the law restricts mining to between 6am and 6pm but illegal miners work at night, and that a local harvester fetches Sh15,000 to Sh20,000 per lorry. Chumo said lorries at Mtembur and Kanyarkwar in West Pokot had destroyed roads and bridges, and cited a UNEP estimate of over 50 billion tonnes of sand and gravel mined yearly.

records.title: Youths find refuge in sand mining after pandemic disruptions
records.titleEn: Youths find refuge in sand mining after pandemic disruptions

records.summary: KNA reports that youths on the lower River Nzoia at Nyadorera, Usonga, Siaya County, turned to sand mining as the coronavirus pandemic hit jobs and once-common fish species disappeared. Harvesters dive without gear and report drownings, typhoid and bilharzia, and asked governments for diving equipment. Chrispinus Ngaywa from Busia said middlemen pay Sh5,500 for a 12-tonne lorry and sell it for Sh17,000 or more, and that harvesters plan to form a union.

records.title: Declining catch: Sand harvesting endangers mudfish in Embu
records.titleEn: Declining catch: Sand harvesting endangers mudfish in Embu
records.location: Embu County, Mbeere South, Mutuobare, Kiromboko harvesting site (River Tana, Embu-Kitui border); Marivwe and Muthanthara in Mbeere North also mentioned
records.summary: The Star reports that sand harvesting on the River Tana at Kiromboko, Mutuobare (Mbeere South, Embu) has degraded mudfish habitat. Fisherman Alfred Musyoki, who trapped fish there about 15 years ago, says faster flows mean fish cannot thrive. Site coordinator Tata Nzule says the site can produce more than 500 lorries of sand a week in the dry season and loads more than 70 lorries a day. A Machakos fish vendor says his daily earnings fell from Sh2,000 and above to less than Sh1,000. Embu NEMA director Boniface Birichi says the activity is desilting to protect the Kiambere hydroelectric dam, while activists call for county regulation.
records.limitations: Volumes are a site coordinator's claim, not measured. Fish-decline link is based on fishermen's and vendors' accounts. No byline is shown on the page. The site lies on the Embu-Kitui border; the record covers the Embu side as described.

records.titleEn: Grains of greed: illegal sand mining in Kenya

records.location: Machakos, Kajiado, Nairobi and Makueni counties
records.summary: In an ENACT Observer article, ISS researcher Mohamed Daghar summarises an ENACT study of illegal sand mining in Machakos, Kajiado, Nairobi and Makueni. It reports up to 500 overloaded 10-tonne sand-tipper trucks leaving Machakos by day and up to 200 leaving Kajiado, excluding night traffic, mainly to supply Nairobi. It describes cartels of brokers, loaders and gangs protected for a fee by state officers, plus child labour and community conflict. It says that of 47 counties only Makueni has a sand policy framework and authority, set up in 2015, which it credits with weeding out cartels in seven years.

records.titleEn: West Pokot launches sand harvesting policy for Kipkomo

records.title: No more harvesting sand at night, says Kitui official
records.titleEn: No more harvesting sand at night, says Kitui official
records.location: Kitui County; Kivou River, Mwingi Central sub-county; Kanyonyoo checkpoint, Nairobi-Garissa highway
records.summary: Kitui Environment executive John Mwendandu told The Star that the Kitui County Sand Utilization and River Basins Conservation Act, 2023, assented by Governor Julius Malombe on March 1, bars harvesting between 6pm and 6am and transport between 8pm and 6am. Night harvesting or transport, or dealing in sand without a licence, attracts a fine of up to Sh2 million or up to two years in jail. The assembly passed the law unanimously on February 28; it cancels all earlier licences, confines harvesting to gazetted sites and sets up caretaker committees. Malombe said the law targets destruction of river basins from unregulated harvesting.

records.title: Karibu Kobala, kijiji ambako watu huishi na wafu
records.titleEn: Welcome to Kobala, the village where people live with the dead
records.location: Homa Bay County, Kobala village / Kobala sub-location (Lake Victoria shore)
records.summary: Taifa Leo reports that in Kobala village, Homa Bay County, sand digging has left deep pits, hanging houses and exposed graves, with coffin parts and human bones surfacing. Resident Willis Omullo said it began 15 years ago when sand extraction intensified, that at least a quarter of the village has been dug up, and that eight houses once stood on land now swamped. He said some digging takes place below the lake water level, and that families themselves dig their own land. Former digger Karen Juma Odera said it took her four days to fill a lorry, for which she was paid Sh1,000.

records.titleEn: Environmental Implications of Sand Harvesting: Insights from Archer's Post, Samburu County
records.publisher: Journal of the Kenya National Commission for UNESCO
records.location: Samburu County, Archer's Post Sub Location (Ewaso Nyiro riverine); sand supplied to Isiolo, Meru and other towns
records.summary: This open-access study by Maasai Mara University researchers assesses drivers and environmental effects of sand harvesting at Archer's Post, Samburu County, where sand is taken from the Ewaso Nyiro riverine in the rainy season and from land in the dry season, and supplied to Isiolo, Meru and other towns. It used a target population of 135 individuals, including residents, harvesters, chiefs and Ministry of Land and NEMA officers. records.title: Impact of Selected Anthropogenic Disturbances on the Variability of Riparian Vegetation in the River Kathita Basin, Tharaka Nithi County, Kenya
records.titleEn: Impact of Selected Anthropogenic Disturbances on the Variability of Riparian Vegetation in the River Kathita Basin, Tharaka Nithi County, Kenya
records.publisher: East African Journal of Environment and Natural Resources (EANSO)
records.authors: Denis Kibaara Mugambi; Rithaa Jafford Njeru; Agatha Nthenge
records.location: Tharaka Nithi County, River Kathita basin
records.summary: This open-access Chuka University study compares riparian vegetation at sand harvesting, charcoal burning and livestock drinking sites with undisturbed control sites, randomly sampled along a 15KM transect, in the River Kathita basin, Tharaka-Nithi County. Disturbed sites showed lower species diversity than undisturbed sites. The correlation with tree diversity was significant for livestock grazing (p=0.01) and marginally insignificant for sand harvesting and charcoal burning (p=0.06). Abandoned sand harvesting sites had high seedling and sapling diversity, suggesting recovery if protected. The authors recommend that local and national stakeholders regulate sand harvesting in riparian areas.
records.limitations: Ecological vegetation study; sand harvesting is one of three disturbances examined, and its statistical association was not significant at p<0.05. No extraction volumes.

records.title: How grassroots resistance fosters sustainability: lessons from sand harvesting and water availability in a farming community in Kenya
records.titleEn: How grassroots resistance fosters sustainability: lessons from sand harvesting and water availability in a farming community in Kenya
records.authors: Annelieke Duker; Diego Zuluaga Velásquez; Pooja Prasad; Charlotte de Fraiture; Gabriela Cuadrado Quesada
records.location: Makueni County; Kasikeu community; Enguli River
records.summary: This open-access Water SA paper by IHE Delft researchers studies how unregulated sand harvesting on the Enguli River, a sand river near Kasikeu in Makueni County draining to the Muooni within the Athi basin, affected smallholder irrigators. Using a baseline survey of 60 farmers and semi-structured interviews, the authors report intensive harvesting between 2012 and 2015, after a district commissioner in 2010 asked Kasikeu leaders to let lorries in. They find excessive harvesting depleted water and forced irrigators to stop farming, and that grassroots resistance pushed the newly decentralised county government to curb sand conflicts and support river restoration under Makueni's Sand Act.

records.summary: Researchers Kennedy Mkutu and Jan Bachmann summarise a study of sand commodity chains at sites in seven Kenyan counties, including Homa Bay near Lake Victoria and Nakuru. They say national regulation is rarely enforced and informal rules among loaders, cooperatives and landowners govern extraction. In Kajiado, a driver pays loaders around $10 each and the landowner $40-$50. They report drivers pay around $90 for a 12-ton truck that sells in Nairobi for up to $400, and police request $4-8 per truck. At Kedong in Nakuru, residents destroyed landowners' excavators. They argue for harmonising informal rules with formal ones, citing Makueni.

It covers both Athi and non-Athi counties and may overlap with Athi-basin records. English translation of the headline awaits Swahili review.

records.summary: NEMA's page on the proposed Environmental Management (Sand Harvesting) Regulations, 2022 explains that EMCA provides for EIA licences for sand harvesting and requires proponents to submit annual audits. NEMA says it was tasked with developing regulations in response to the provisions of part V section 42 (4) of EMCA 1999, to streamline the activity nationwide and make it a sustainable industry. The stated objectives are sustainable use of the sand resource, sound environmental management, and reduced environmental damage alongside socio-economic benefits. The page invites people likely to be affected to submit written comments.
